full_judgment: 7. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that the petitioners got certified copy of the judgment dated 19.12.1957 passed in Second Appeal No.476 of 1954 on 15.04.2015 and therefore, it could not be produced earlier to remove doubt as to the genuineness of the decree passed in Rent Suit No.59 of 1952 and for these reasons the impugned judgment was required to be reviewed. He further submitted that the judgment in Second Appeal No. 476 of 1954 showed that the question of landlord and tenant relationship was considered earlier and was finally decided by judgment and decree dated 16.06.1959 dismissing the present suit questioning the right of Anisuzzaman Khandoker and others for filing the rent suit. He further submitted that the suit was dismissed holding that the auction sale in Rent Execution Case No. 85 of 1961 was not permissible in law after acquisition of rent receiving interest. But by section 68C of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, right to institute and continue the rent suit and the rent execution case was given afresh which was not taken into consideration. He further submitted that after auction filing of Rent Execution Case No. 85 of 1961, judgment-debtor, Binod Behari Golder, contested the case by filing Objection Miscellaneous Case No. 220 of 1961 and Miscellaneous Appeal No. 16 of 1962 and thereafter, 11.58 acres land was sold in auction which was brushed aside only on suspicion. He further submitted that delay in mutating name by the auction purchaser was taken into consideration for disbelieving auction purchase dated 11.11.1963 by Kazi Shamsujjoha. But filing Title Suit No. 639 of 1966 by judgment-debtor, Binod Behari Golder, Miscellaneous Case No. 126 of 1966 for setting aside sale, Miscellaneous Case No. 18 of 1968 for setting aside the ex-perte order setting aside sale and continuance of litigation up to 16.10.1969 was not taken into consideration. He further submitted that the decision in the case of Abdul Hamid and others-Vs-Ali Baksh Mondol and others reported in 20 DLR 699 was a judgment per in curiam in view of the provision of section 68C of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. He further submitted that the investigation report in C.R. Case No.4029 of 2009 found that the certificate sale of 5.06 acres land in Certificate Case No.7BKB/79-80 was totally false. The petitioners proved their title and possession by producing registered certificate of sale of land, writ of delivery of possession, series of registered barga kabuliyat, order of mutation of name in SA Khatian and payment of rent to Government continuously for more than 25 years by producing series of rent receipts, but these evidence was not at all considered at any stage.
